newsitem.title: UK: Germany's total cocoa consumption 323,000 T in 95/96.
newsitem.headline: Germany's total cocoa consumption 323,000 T in 95/96.

text.p: Germany's consumption of cocoa beans, including imports and exports of semi-finished products, totalled 323,813 tonnes bean equivalent in the 1995/96 (Oct/Sept) season, a study carried out by the confectionery industry association BDS showed.

Karsten Keunecke, managing director of BDS, said on Wednesday, the excess over the total grindings of 287,519 tonnes mainly stemmed from net impots of cocoa butter of 79,355 tonnes of bean equivalent.

But the analysis also discounted for a total 43,933 tonnes of net cocoa liquor/paste exports and 8,879 tonnes of net cocoa cake exports which were deducted from consumption, Keunecke said on the sidelines of a meeting of the International Cocoa Organization(ICCO).
Net cocoa powder imports were 9,751 tonnes of bean equivalent.
Keunecke said the study showed that grinding figures did not reflect the true level of German cocoa consumption.
Traders have been sceptical over the accuracy over German grindings data which they said was resulting in lower stock figures.
Cocoa imports into Germany have significantly exceeded domestic grindings in the last five years.
But Keunecke said in the past that lower grinding figures were a result of a shift of processing to the Netherlands and producer countries.
